transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-09
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (Acme - Head of ML), Mark Rivera (Acme - Infrastructure), Priya Shah (Acme - Prod)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly caching sync. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Dana: Dana here.
[00:07] Mark: Mark here.
[00:09] Priya: Priya here.
[00:12] Lena: Lena from Redwood.
[00:14] Samir: Awesome. I'll hand it to Lena to run through the metrics, we pulled the latest from the pilot cluster.

[02:10] Lena: Okay so overview — week over week we see overall token cost down by about 7% with caching on, but hit patterns are mixed. Our prefix cache hit is around 42% on the top 1K prompts, KV cache hit steady at ~67%. Those are rough numbers, there's noise in the sampling window. Prefix is lower than we expected.

[03:00] Dana: Wait 42%? last week we had reported 58% on a smaller sample, did something regress?

[03:10] Lena: Good question. I think two factors: one, prompt canonicalization wasn't applied consistently — different punctuation and whitespace created distinct keys; two, we discovered the keying layer hashed the entire prompt including dynamic values like timestamps and user ids for some routes. So collisions are low but effective reuse drops.

[04:00] Mark: We also injected a new frontend that prepends session metadata to prompts for logging, that likely changed the prefix seen by the cache.

[04:20] Priya: Right — some product flows append product ids. We thought those would be stripped but ok.

[05:00] Samir: Good catch. So canonicalization + normalization should help. Lena, do you have proposed changes?

[05:10] Lena: Yes. Plan A: deterministic canonicalization — strip PII-like fields, normalize whitespace, lowercasing where safe, remove ephemeral tokens. Use a stable prefix extractor for conversational context (first N tokens) rather than whole prompt hashing. Plan B: fall back to embedding-based fuzzy matching for near duplicates for routes where exact keying loses too much. We tested a small run showing embedding fuzzy match recovers additional ~10-12% hit rate but costs more CPU on the control plane.

[06:15] Dana: Embedding fuzzy matching worries me a bit re: determinism — we need strong reproducibility for our acceptance tests. Is fuzzy only for non-critical routes?

[06:30] Lena: Exactly — fuzzy would be optional and route-configurable. Our proposal: critical flows use deterministic keying; lower-risk exploration UIs use fuzzy match to boost perceived cache hit.

[07:00] Samir: How about TTL / eviction policy — anything there affecting numbers?

[07:10] Lena: TTL currently set to 24 hours for prefix keys, 72 hours for KV entries. We saw a handful of high-cardinality keys evicting quickly because of a small cache size allocation per route. If we increase per-route capacity we get higher hit but cost rises. We ran a simulation: doubling prefix cache capacity improved hit from 42% -> 57% for that route, but per-token cost increased ~4% due to memory footprint.

[08:00] Mark: Memory on the pilot GPUs is limited; if we move to Dedicated we can provision higher KV store limits, but need to justify cost.

[08:25] Priya: From product side, what's our target hit rate to consider this a win?

[08:30] Dana: For our throughput and SLOs, we'd like to see overall prefix+KV effective reuse >70% on the canonical prompt set, with latency improvement to <150ms p50.

[09:00] Lena: On latency — cache hit typically reduces inference time by ~30-50ms per call for small models, more for larger. But note, embedding-based fuzzy lookup adds ~20-30ms if run synchronously; we can make it async for user-visible UIs.

[10:15] Samir: Let's talk instrumentation. Are the metrics we have sufficient to debug key misses?

[10:25] Lena: We have per-route hit/miss counters, and we log the normalized key and a hashed token for matched entries. But we don't yet log the pre/post canonicalization delta frequently — i.e., how often canonicalization changed a key. I recommend increasing sampling to capture mismatches and examples for the top 500 misses.

[11:00] Dana: Can you add an export of sample misses so our team can annotate and decide canonicalization rules?

[11:10] Lena: Yes, we'll add a sampled dump (redact PII) and a small UI with examples. Samir will share spreadsheet to track the mapping.

[12:00] Samir: On the security/compliance side, anything flagged by logs or retention?

[12:10] Mark: We need clarity on how long Redis keys persist in logs and whether cache keys include any PII. If canonicalization removes PII we should be ok. Also need to confirm KMS key management if we go Dedicated.

[12:40] Lena: We'll coordinate with security. Canonicalization will drop obvious PII; cache logs will store only hashed keys and route ids.

[13:10] Priya: Back to tradeoffs — is it better to prioritize prefix normalization or capacity increase?

[13:20] Lena: Normalization is low-cost and likely gives the most immediate lift. Capacity increase helps but has recurring cost. So short term normalize + fix keying; mid-term run fuzzy matching for specific routes; long-term evaluate Dedicated for capacity/throughput.

[15:00] Dana: Sounds reasonable. Can we set concrete experiments this week?

[15:10] Samir: Yes — Lena will push keying patch to pilot and run 24h test, Samir will update the benchmark spreadsheet to include before/after and per-route cost delta, Dana will provide canonical prompt set. We'll reconvene next week with results.

[16:05] Mark: One quick ask — can Redwood surface which model variant served a cached response? We want to ensure model variant parity for cached items.

[16:20] Lena: We attach model variant id in cache metadata currently; we'll make it visible in the dashboard per-route.

[17:00] Samir: Any other blockers?

[17:05] Dana: Nothing else on my side.

[17:20] Priya: I'm good.

[17:30] Samir: Great. To recap — immediate: canonicalization + key patch, sample miss export, update benchmarks, confirm infra constraints and security notes. Next sync same time next week. Samir will send meeting notes and links.

[18:00] Lena: I'll also include a short doc with recommended canonicalization rules and example transforms.

[18:20] Samir: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

[END]
